title: Portfolio concierge
intro: I answer questions about Natalia's work: outcomes, how she builds design operating systems, AI tooling, team leadership and availability. Ask anything, or start from one of these.
footnote: Answers come from a knowledge file Natalia writes. If it isn't in there, I say so instead of guessing.
noMatch: That one isn't in Natalia's knowledge file, so I won't guess at it. Try one of the questions below, or write to her directly at dicrearte@gmail.com.

entries.question: What has she actually shipped?
entries.answer: Five cases carry it. VIU — a 73-component design system with verified Figma-to-code parity, built solo. Elastic's pricing hub redesign — +59.5% Cloud signups and 89% engagement on the Hosted path. An AI-native UX portfolio of seven initiatives projected to return 2,600–4,500 hours a year. At VMware, +67% production efficiency across 7 regional stores and +9% global conversion. At Palo Alto Networks, a design system and an accessibility-first color system, both adopted as foundational.

entries.question: How does she use AI day to day?
entries.answer: As an executor she directs, not an autonomous generator. She built VIU by delegating execution to Claude under skills she designed and governs herself, with a pre-flight check that forces verification of Figma's real state before every change. At Elastic she defined and led seven AI-powered UX initiatives and a Design Ready / UX QA gate, so AI output has to clear a senior bar before it ships.

entries.question: What is she looking for?
entries.answer: Manager, Director or Head of UX roles — the same line runs across the top of this site. She is most useful where design has to scale through systems and governance rather than headcount: global B2B web, enterprise SaaS, design systems and design ops.

entries.question: How do I contact her?
entries.answer: Email dicrearte@gmail.com, WhatsApp +506 8719 4296, or LinkedIn at linkedin.com/in/nataliars. Her work is also on Behance at behance.net/Natalia_R_S. Those are the same icons sitting in this site's header.

entries.question: How does she build design operating systems?
entries.answer: By putting the standard in infrastructure instead of in her own review queue. At Elastic that meant a Web UX Operating Model of five programs that made roughly 140 page deliveries a year predictable, plus a Web UX Playbook adopted by Engineering, PMM, Brand, SEO and Localization. The test she applies to her own work: it should not depend on her reviewing every piece.

entries.question: How does she lead a team?
entries.answer: Systems over centralization, governance over arbitration, player-coach over coordinator. She ran an individual gap analysis with each person, weekly 1:1 coaching and group sessions to integrate the team as a unit. Over her tenure the team grew from design-only into optimization, UX engineering and full ownership of the design system and Storybook — and when the company mandated AI adoption in 2026, UX produced the strongest innovations in the organization.

entries.question: What is VIU?
entries.answer: Her own design system — and the one this site is built with. 73 Figma components (29 atoms, 35 molecules, 9 organisms, 4 patterns), the @viu/ui React library, a Storybook themed as a product with a per-component accessibility check, and design tokens whose parity with Figma is verified by scripts. Built solo, over one calendar month of intermittent work.

entries.question: What did she do at Elastic?
entries.answer: She owned UX strategy, design systems, research operations and AI-native workflows for elastic.co as Senior Manager, UX & Design. The pricing hub redesign replaced a single-product landing page with a centralized hub across Self-managed, Serverless and Hosted, and delivered +59.5% Cloud signups — Elastic's primary growth metric — with 89% engagement on the Hosted path.

entries.question: How much experience does she have?
entries.answer: 18+ years, from a first creative lead role in regional e-commerce to building the web experience org at a global infrastructure company. Four global platforms led, four design systems built, 11 languages shipped, and 5M+ monthly reach at her peak platform. The About page carries every role in full.

entries.question: How does she handle accessibility?
entries.answer: As a floor, not a feature. In VIU every component carries a contrast audit against WCAG 2.2 AA with real numbers — success-solid.light moved from green.600 to green.700 to reach 7.48:1 — and border-contrast exceptions are documented under WCAG 1.4.11 instead of quietly ignored. At Palo Alto Networks she built an accessibility-focused color system adopted across paloaltonetworks.com.

entries.question: What tools does she work in?
entries.answer: Figma with MCP, Storybook, React, Claude and Claude Code, Maze, Adobe Target, Optimizely, Magento, AEM and Marketo. She still builds hands-on — HTML, CSS and JavaScript are part of the job, not a past life.

entries.question: Where is she based?
entries.answer: Costa Rica. Her whole career has been on global teams — coordinating parallel workstreams across companies, regions and time zones at VMware, and working with teams across Asia, Europe and the Americas.

entries.question: What languages does she speak?
entries.answer: Spanish is her native language and she works professionally in English. This site runs in both — the globe in the header switches it.

entries.question: Can I see her resume?
entries.answer: The Resume button in the header and in the footer has it. The About page carries the same material in full: every role, skills, education and certifications.
